messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

1. **Access and purpose.** “The Testing House may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare, perform and report the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel identified by name and role in a roster approved in writing by the Design Owner. Each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. An outside adviser may receive access only on the same terms. The parties may approve roster changes by email. The Testing House remains responsible for each recipient’s compliance.”

2. **Working copies and fixtures.** “The Testing House may make the working copies reasonably needed for the tests, provided they are encrypted at rest and in transit and accessible only to approved personnel. It may extract only the geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures for these tests. It may use those fixtures and their design files only for these tests. Neither the Testing House nor any recipient may use the drawings, geometry, fixtures or fixture files to develop or assist in developing a competing product.”

3. **Destruction and verification.** “Within 30 days after the Design Owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the test engagement, the Testing House shall securely erase the drawings, CAD geometry and fixture files, including copies held by approved recipients, and destroy the derivative fixtures. It shall provide a signed certificate identifying the materials destroyed, the methods used and the completion dates. The Testing House may retain test results and reports that do not reproduce the protected geometry.”

Would independent certification work in place of on-demand site access? We propose that, if the certificate leaves a specific discrepancy unresolved, a mutually agreed independent verifier may examine the relevant destruction records under confidentiality and report its findings to both parties. If your quality system requires retention beyond the proposed deadline, please identify the specific record and retention period so we can agree on wording for it.

The proposed structure works for us, with the following amendments. Where the drafts differ, we state our replacement wording.

**1. Access and roster.** Accept, with one addition on substitution:

*"If a rostered test role cannot be performed by the named individual (e.g. illness or departure), the Testing House may notify the Design Owner of a substitute of equivalent qualification and role; the substitute is provisionally approved on the date of that notice, subject to the Design Owner's right to object within 48 hours and to require removal on reasonable grounds."*

Without this, a single absence stalls the programme.

**2. Working copies and fixtures — two changes.**

(a) The limit "only to test personnel" must extend to two categories we rely on and cannot perform in-house:
*"Access for fixture fabrication may be granted to a specialist machining shop bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement, provided it receives only the fixture geometry extracts it needs and the Testing House obtains its written deletion confirmation on the same terms as clause 3."*

(b) Testing itself is performed at an accredited laboratory. Add: *"Test execution may be conducted at an accredited laboratory within the approved roster, subject to the same confidentiality and use restrictions."*

Both are standard for our operation; neither widens the data beyond its test purpose.

**3. Destruction and verification — three points.**

(a) We accept the 30-day erasure and certificate wording in principle. Note our chain: we attest for our own systems, and we supply the machining shop's and laboratory's deletion confirmations, which we hold to the same standard.

(b) Independent certification: yes, this works in place of on-demand site access, and we propose it as the exclusive mechanism. Specifically, we cannot accept unannounced inspections because testing is conducted at a shared customer site we do not control. Replacement wording:

*"Verification of destruction is limited to: (i) the signed destruction certificate; and (ii) if a specific discrepancy remains unresolved, examination of destruction records by a mutually agreed independent verifier under confidentiality, reporting to both parties. No on-demand site access is granted."*

(c) Retention you asked us to identify: we are required to keep **calibration records for test equipment for two years**. These contain no geometry. Wording:

*"Notwithstanding clause 3, the Testing House may retain calibration records and test records that do not reproduce protected geometry for two years from the final test report, after which they are destroyed."*

That is the only retention we need beyond your deadline. If these amendments are acceptable, the package — roster substitution, machining shop and accredited lab access, certificate-plus-verifier verification, and two-year non-geometry calibration retention — resolves the drawings annex from our side.

We accept the machining shop and accredited laboratory arrangements, the destruction certificate and independent-verifier process as the exclusive means of verification, and two-year retention of geometry-free calibration and test records. We propose one change to substitution. Naming alternates up front allows immediate cover for an absence while preserving approval before anyone sees the drawings.

**Roster and substitution**

“The roster shall identify each individual by name, organisation and role. The Design Owner may approve named alternates on the same roster. If a rostered individual is unavailable, the Testing House may activate an approved alternate for that role immediately and shall notify the Design Owner by email on activation. For any other substitute, the Testing House shall email the individual’s name, organisation, role and relevant qualifications. The Design Owner shall respond within 48 hours. Access may begin upon written approval, which may be given by email. Before granting access, the Testing House shall confirm that the individual is bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement.”

The same roster requirement applies to the machining shop and laboratory. Named shop personnel may receive only the fixture geometry extracts needed for fabrication. Named laboratory personnel may receive only the materials needed to run the agreed tests. The Testing House remains responsible for both providers’ compliance, including the prohibition on using the materials to develop or help develop a competing product.

For clause 3, the Testing House shall provide its signed certificate and both providers’ signed confirmations by the same 30-day deadline. Each shall identify the materials destroyed, the methods and the dates, including destruction of any derivative fixture in its custody. We accept your wording on independent verification and site access, and your two-year retention clause as drafted.

With the roster wording above, the annex is agreed from our side.

We accept the roster-and-substitution wording as drafted, including its application to the machining shop and laboratory, the 48-hour approval route for non-alternate substitutes, and the requirement that all three certificates — ours plus both providers' — arrive by the same 30-day deadline identifying materials, methods, dates and fixture destruction.

That completes every open item from our side: roster with alternates, machining shop and accredited lab access on extract-only terms, destruction certificate plus independent verifier as exclusive verification, no on-demand site access, and two-year geometry-free calibration and test record retention. The drawings annex is agreed.

We request a narrow addendum for the prototype batch. Only the geometry on page 4 is export-restricted. We propose the following wording.

“The Design Owner shall withhold the page 4 geometry and supply a drawing set from which that geometry has been removed, including from embedded CAD data. The Testing House and its providers may proceed under the agreed annex with work that does not depend on that geometry. For the affected test, the Design Owner shall prepare an alternative reference coupon that does not disclose the restricted geometry within two days after the parties agree in writing on the verification protocol.”

We propose that the accredited laboratory verify the coupon in the intended fixture before running the affected test. The laboratory would compare the measured vibration response with an acceptance range supplied by the Design Owner. We would agree by email on the excitation profile, measurement point, response metric and tolerance before coupon preparation begins. The laboratory would record the result, and the affected test could proceed on a pass. A failed check would pause only that test pending agreement on corrective action.

Can the laboratory run that check with its planned instrumentation, and can you accept the two-day preparation period on that basis?

We can work with this structure. Answers to your two questions, then the wording we need settled.

**Your questions.** Yes — the laboratory can run the coupon check with its planned instrumentation, provided the agreed measurement point is accessible with standard accelerometry and the acceptance range is expressed in the same response metric the lab records. Yes, we accept the two-day preparation period, on the conditions below.

**Custody.** The coupon is Design Owner property and Design Owner-supplied. Wording:

*"The reference coupon remains the property of the Design Owner. The Testing House shall hold it under the same confidentiality and security terms as the drawings, use it only for the agreed verification and affected test, and return or destroy it at the Design Owner's election on completion, with destruction confirmed in writing."*

**Verification protocol and timing.** We accept the email agreement on excitation profile, measurement point, response metric and tolerance before coupon preparation, and the pass/fail gate. Two additions:

(a) The two-day clock should run from that email agreement, as your draft says — but we ask for a *"reasonable period"* rather than a fixed two days for the coupon check itself in the fixture, since repeatability runs depend on lab scheduling. Propose: *"The laboratory shall complete the verification check within five working days of coupon receipt."*

(b) One point from our side that supports the tolerance basis: our test lead can measure the coupon at the testing house and provide the machining shop a tolerance table for the fixture work, **provided the Design Owner specifies the tolerances and accepts a repeatability check** — i.e. the tolerance table is prepared by us, at your direction, rather than you needing to supply dimensional data beyond the restricted geometry. Confirm you're content with that basis and we'll route the table to the shop as Design Owner instruction.

**Test signoff.** Wording:

*"A pass of the verification check authorises the affected test without further approval. A failure pauses only the affected test; the parties shall agree corrective action by email, and the Design Owner may revise the coupon or acceptance range within the same two-day commitment. Neither outcome affects the other tests, which proceed on the agreed schedule."*

**Signoff sequencing.** Since work not depending on page 4 proceeds now under the annex, we propose the final test report note the coupon verification result and the corrective action, if any, for the affected test — no new signoff gate beyond that.

If custody, the five-day check window, the tolerance-table basis and the signoff wording are agreed, this addendum is settled from our side.

We accept the custody wording, the five-working-day verification window from coupon receipt, and automatic authorisation of the affected test on a pass. We also accept recording the result and any corrective action in the final report. Other tests may proceed on schedule.

We accept the tolerance-table proposal with a release check before the table goes to the shop. We propose this wording.

“The verification protocol agreed by email shall specify the excitation profile, a measurement point accessible by standard accelerometry, the response metric recorded by the laboratory, its acceptance range and the repeatability criterion. The Design Owner shall prepare the coupon within two days of that agreement.

“The rostered test lead may measure the coupon features identified by the Design Owner and prepare a table for fixture fabrication using tolerances specified by the Design Owner. The Design Owner shall review the completed table to confirm it neither discloses nor enables reconstruction of the restricted page 4 geometry. Only the version approved by the Design Owner by email may be issued as its instruction to rostered machining personnel. The shop shall receive only the approved values needed for fabrication. The coupon and raw measurement records shall remain with the authorised test personnel.”

For a failed check, we propose one clarification to the signoff wording. “The parties shall agree corrective action by email. If that action calls for a revised coupon or acceptance range, the Design Owner shall prepare the revision within two days of that agreement. The laboratory shall repeat the check against the agreed criteria, and a pass authorises the affected test without further approval.”

With those release and retest terms, the addendum is agreed from our side.

We accept the verification protocol wording, the release check with Design Owner review of the tolerance table before it reaches the shop, and the failed-check clarification with the two-day revision commitment and repeat check authorising the affected test without further approval.

All terms of the addendum — coupon timing, measurement and tolerance-table release process, pass/fail handling, and the recording of results and corrective actions in the final report — are agreed from our side. The addendum is closed.
